pr_title: Improve serialization of GrainReference when using JSON
pr_body:
Fixes #3063.

We have a specific `JsonConverter` for grain references which was introduced along with the non-static `SerializationManager` changes. The converter is required to flow the runtime context into `GrainReferences` on .NET Standard, but it was incorrectly implemented.

On full .NET, this converter is technically not required, since `GrainReference` implements `ISerializable` and we flow the runtime into the `StreamingContext.Context` property. This property does not exist on .NET Standard < v2.0 and so this converter is required.

This PR involves a rewrite of the implementation of `GrainReferenceConverter` so that GrainReferences work even if they are passed via a field with an ambiguous type such as `object` or `GrainReference`.

It does this by having an internal serializer which defers to the `ISerializable` implementation, and then manually binding the reference to the runtime at deserialization time.

issue_context.title: NullReferenceException roundtrip GrainReference with jsonserializer
comments:
That does seem like a bug, thanks for tracking it down, @rikbosch.

From what I can tell initially, the concrete type information of the GrainReference is not being serialized, and this is what's causing the issue on deserialization. If we were to serialize the ref as a json object instead of as a string, maybe JSON.NET would be able to insert concrete type information into the object.
I'm not into that much details on this one, but would this occur in every storage provider or just the ADO.NET one?

@rikace it's because the type is `GrainReference` and not the concrete, runtime implementation of the grain reference. I'm still looking into the fix. Fixing it on full .NET is simple, since we can just remove that serializer and use the `ISerializable` implementation in `GrainReference`. On .NET Standard (for 2.0 builds), we cannot rely on `ISerializable`, however, since `StreamingContext` is unusable (has no `Context` property for us to flow the runtime through). So I'm looking into the best way to fix this for both platforms.
